ops.title: Google style guide layer: scope, supersession semantics, and deliberate exclusions
ops.body:
## What landed

The Google developer documentation style guide (https://developers.google.com/style, CC BY 4.0) is ported into a third rule layer, `google`, alongside `slop` and `base`. 169 rules: 136 client-side detectors, 29 sentence-tier, 4 document-tier. Catalogue is now 226 rules (178 client-side, 40 sentence, 8 document).

## Decisions worth not relitigating

**Supersession is span-scoped, not blanket.** `rules.Supersedes` maps a google rule to the rule IDs it silences, and `dropSuperseded` in `cmd/slop-cop/check.go` only silences a rule on spans where the superseding google rule actually fired. A blanket override was built first and was wrong: `colon-elaboration` is a genuine LLM tell in `The result: chaos.` but mandatory Google style in `Run the following command:`. Blanket-silencing loses the tell; blanket-protecting double-reports on correct docs. Span scoping resolves both and makes the owner's requirement ("Google overrides except the LLM slop triggers") structural rather than a maintained list.

**A per-rule protected set was tried and discarded.** Protection turned out to be per-*pair*, not per-rule: `em-dash-pivot` is correctly superseded by `number-range-hyphen` (a range is not a pivot) but protected against `parenthetical-example-at-end`. A `ProtectedTells` set could not express that, so it was deleted in favour of span scoping.

**Nothing in the repo is frozen.** `internal/rules/rules.go` and its siblings are recorded in NOTICE as *derived from* awnist/slop-cop; that is provenance documentation, not an edit prohibition. An earlier read of AGENTS.md treated "must stay byte-untouched" as binding and shaped the design around it. The owner corrected this. The layer still ended up purely additive, but by choice, not constraint.

**Scope cut from 337 to 169 by general-prose relevance.** Extraction yielded 337 candidate rules; every one was scored 1-5 for relevance to the prose slop-cop actually lints (READMEs, blog posts, PR descriptions, commit messages). Dropped: example-data hygiene (credit-card Luhn checks, IP addresses, phone numbers, street addresses), mathematical notation, `@param` doc-comment mechanics, image/figure/caption markup, and formatter-owned mechanics. 12 high-value rules that were noisy only because a *regex* cannot judge them (`ambiguous-pronoun`, `context-before-instruction`) were re-tiered to the LLM sentence pass rather than dropped.

**Inclusive-language and ableist-terminology guidance is excluded by owner decision.** This is a scoping call about what the linter ships, not a judgement about the guidance. NOTICE says so plainly and points readers to the guide. Do not add it back without asking.

## Traps

- `All = Slop + Base + Google` order is load-bearing. `buildRulePrompt` numbers rules by position, so a fourth layer must append last or every prompt golden shifts.
- Shard-prefixed identifiers (`punct1reSerialComma`) in `internal/detectors/google_*.go` exist because 20 agents wrote the package concurrently. Keep the convention.
- README rule counts are hand-maintained. No CI job checks them against `len(rules.All)`.
- Measured false-positive rate after the first implementation pass was roughly 40% on markdown, concentrated in three detectors that misread markdown structure (GitHub `[!WARNING]` alert syntax, all-caps filenames like NOTICE, identifiers already inside link text). Density on clean markdown is ~2.4 violations/KB.
</body>
